{{Short description|American mathematician (1944–2024)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2024}}
'''Roger Keith Dennis''' (March 10, 1944 – December 12, 2024), known as '''R. Keith Dennis''' or '''Keith Dennis''', was an American mathematician who worked in [[algebraic K-theory]] and [[group theory]].  His career was spent as a professor in the Department of Mathematics at [[Cornell University]].  Dennis was the executive editor of ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' as it transitioned from a printed resource to a mainly-digital one.

==Early life and career==
Dennis was born in [[Vernon, Texas]], on March 10, 1944, and grew up on a farm 8 miles north of [[Quanah, Texas]]. He graduated from [[Quanah High School]] in 1962, and attended [[Rice University]], earning his bachelor's in 1966 and his doctorate in 1970.<ref name=cornellobit/><ref name=cortacaobit/>  His thesis on "Presentation for the Elementary Group and the Functor <math>K_2</math>" was done under [[Stephen M. Gersten]].<ref name=mgp/>  He spent the academic year 1970–1971 at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton as the first assistant of [[John Milnor]].<ref name=cornellobit/><ref name=ias>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/roger-keith-dennis Roger Keith Dennis]  Member: School of Mathematics 9/1970 – 8/1971, IAS</ref>

In 1971, Dennis joined the Department of Mathematics at Cornell University, and he was promoted to full professor in 1981. From 1987 to 1993 he served as the department chair.  He retired to emeritus status in 2019.<ref name=cornellobit/>

From January 1995 through June 1998, Dennis was the executive editor of the American Mathematical Society’s ''Mathematical Reviews''.<ref name=ams/> During this period ''Mathematical Reviews'' designed and began the development of [[MathSciNet]]<ref name=cornellobit/><ref name=globalmathlib/> which went online in January 1996.

He was on the Board of Advisors of the [[American Institute of Mathematics]] since its inception.<ref name=aim_board_1/><ref name=aim_board_2/>

In 2013, Dennis was in the inaugural class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name=fellows/>

==Personal life and death==
Dennis had four children. He died of metastatic [[prostate cancer]] on December 12, 2024, at the age of 80.<ref name=cornellobit/><ref name=cortacaobit/>

==Books==
* 1982 (editor) ''Algebraic K-Theory.  Proceedings of a Conference Held at Oberwolfach, June 1980'', [https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/BFb0062163 Part 1] and [https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/BFb0061896 Part 2].  (Springer)
* 1993 (with [[Benson Farb]]) ''[https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-0889-1 Noncommutative Algebra] (Springer, Graduate Texts in Mathematics Book 144)'', August 20, 1993, {{ISBN | 978-0-387-94057-1}}
